title_as_printed: Clinical observation of VR virtual reality rehabilitation training combined with acupuncture in the treatment of mild cognitive impairment

Task_Type.reason: Two-arm randomised clinical trial (VR training + scalp/eye acupuncture vs VR training alone) with MMSE/MoCA outcomes.
Task_Type.quote: The treatment group received VR rehabilitation training combined with acupuncture treatment, while the control group received VR training only.

Category.reason: Clinical trial with neuropsychological outcome scales. An EEG FBCSP algorithm is described for the VR/BCI system design, but no EEG data are analysed or reported.
Category.quote: The MMSE and MoCA scales are the main scales for measuring MCI.

Validation_Type.reason: Trial; no predictive model is validated (convention V2).

Sample_N_Approx.reason: The paper reports 48 randomised and 46 who completed and were analysed (Tables 4-7 use n = 23 per arm). The registry uses the randomised figure without saying so.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: In this paper, 48 MCI patients admitted to the hospital were randomly assigned to the control group and the treatment group [p.7] ... a total of 46 cases were effectively completed. [p.8]

notes: Identity check: title_in_pdf_map ('Clinical efficacy of virtual reality rehabilitation training combined with acupuncture at head points for mild cognitive...') is not the printed title, but the map's DOI (10.1016/j.slast.2025.100250) matches the PDF, Crossref returns the printed title for that DOI, and a Crossref title search finds no other paper with the map title, so the PDF is the right document and the map title is a paraphrase. Paper-quality flags (do not change the codes): Table 3 counts 28 (13 M + 15 F) treatment and 18 (10 + 8) control participants against 24/24 randomised; a 'meta-analysis' (OR = 2.74, WMD = 2.42) is applied to this single two-arm trial; Table 2 'Deletion' total is 0 against 1 + 1 dropouts.
